texts.facts: 1. These two claim petitions are filed by two claimants under Section 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for grant of compensation. 2. Both these two claim petitions have arisen out of same accident. Therefore, both of them were clubbed for the purposes of adjudication and disposal and it was decided that the case of "Chanderwati Vs. Rajiv Kumar" shall be treated as the leading case and evidence recorded in the case of "Smt. Chanderwati" shall be read in evidence in connected claim petition of "Shri Ravinder" as well. 3. Respondent No. 1 is the driver, Respondent No. 2 is the Owner and Respondent No. 3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Facts in the case of Smt. Chander Wati: 4. It is stated in this claim petition that on 09.03.2010, at about 4:15 hours, petitioner along with her nephew, Sh. Ravinder was going towards village Himayupur on Motorcycle bearing No. DL4S BK1113 and when they reached near Pochanpur Temple, Dwarka, New Delhi, all of a sudden the offending vehicle bearing No.DL 2CAK9618 came at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, without safety of others and hit their motorcycle as a result of which both of them fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries. 5. It is stated that the petitioner was taken to Trauma Centre AIIMS where she remained admitted as an indoor patient. Shri Ravinder vs Shri Rajeev Kumar (Driver) on 5 February, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172549522/ 2 6. It is stated that FIR No. 60/10 under Sections 279/338 of IPC is registered at P.S. Kapashera against Respondent No. 1. 7. This petitioner has claimed from the respondents a compensation of Rs. 15,00,000/ with pendentlite interest from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization. 8. Respondent No. 1 and 2 have filed a common written statement and have stated that claimant has claimed excessive compensation based on false and concocted story and claim petition is liable to be dismissed. 9. It is also stated that Respondent No. 1 was having a valid driving license and Respondent No. 2 had insured the vehicle and it is also stated that accident is not as a result of rash and negligent driving of Respondent No. 1. 10. Insurance company also filed its written statement and stated that it will have no liability in case driver was not having a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident. 11. Insurance company reserved its rights to take all pleas available under Section 147 and 149 of M.V. Act, if it was held at any stage that the driver of the offending vehicle was under influence of alcohol and violated terms and conditions of policy. 12. Rest of the contents of claim petition were denied but it was admitted that vehicle was insured on the date of accident by the answering insurance company. 13. Facts in the case of Shri Ravinder are similar visa vis sequence of events that which led to the accident as are already noted in the case of Smt. Chander Wati. 14. This petitioner has claimed a compensation of Rs. 15,00,000/ with pendentelite interest from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization. 15. Defence of all the respondents is similar to the defence already taken and noted in preceding paragraphs in the case of Smt. Chander Wati. 16. From the pleadings of parties, following consolidated issues were framed: 1. Whether Smt. Chanderwati in petition no. 91/10 and Shri Ravinder in petition no. 92/10, sustained injuries on their persons in an accident which took place on 09.03.2010 caused due to negligent driving of vehicle bearing registration number DL2CAK9618 being driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3? ..... 3. Relief. 17. First witness to enter in the witness box was Shri Ravinder as PW1 who stated similar facts in his evidence by way of affidavit as were already stated by him in his claim petition. He deposed that he has spent Rs. 2,15,519/ on his medical treatment. Bills for purchase of medicines and his treatment record were proved as Ex. PW1/165 and Voter Card as Ex. PW1/67. He deposed that he has spent Rs. 1 lac on special diet during his treatment. 18. Additionally, he deposed that he is unable to carry on normal work and he has engaged an attendant to whom he is paying Rs. 4,000/ per month. 19. In crossexamination conducted by counsel for Respondent No. 1 and 2, he denied a suggestion that the offending vehicle was Indica Car and not Maruti Swift Car which is shown as the offending vehicle in the claim petition. 20. In crossexamination by counsel for the insurance company, he deposed that he is a farmer by profession and earned Rs. 6,00,000/ in six months time. He deposed that some of the land on which he does farming belongs to him and some land was taken on rent for farming purposes. Theirs is a joint family and the land belongs to the joint family where all the four brothers work together. He clarified that income of Rs. 6,00,000/ is of joint family by doing farming on their agricultural land but he had no documentary evidence to show income from agriculture. 21. Rest of the suggestions contrary to his case were also denied by him. 22. This witness filed his additional evidence by way of affidavit and further proved medical bills as Ex. PW1/67102 and as Ex. PW1/103150 receipts of commission which he used to get on supply by vegetables in the vegetable's market 23. Revenue record showing total holding of agriculture land was exhibited as Ex. PX and disability certificate received from AIIMS by this claimant was proved as Ex. P1. 24. Second witness who entered in the witness box was Smt. Chander Wati as PW2, she stated similar facts in her evidence by way of affidavit as were already stated by her in her claim petition. She also relied on Ex.PW2/122 which are receipts of chemists for purchase of medicines and her Voter Card as Ex. PW2/23. 25. Smt. Chander Wati also entered in the witness box second time and prove discharge summary of AIIMS where she had remained admitted after the accident and few remaining bills as Ex. PW1/Z collectively. Shri Ravinder vs Shri Rajeev Kumar (Driver) on 5 February, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172549522/ 4 26. Third witness examined by claimants was Dr. Ratandeep Bose, Sr. Resident Neurosurgery, JPN Trauma Centre, AIIMS, New Delhi who proved disability certificate in favour of Shri Ravinder which was already exhibited as Ex. P1. 27. Same is the evidence of PW4 Dr. Subodh Associate Professor, AIIMS, New Delhi. 28. No other witness was examined by the petitioners and no witness was examined on behalf of any other respondents. 67. Therefore, for Pain and Suffering, this petitioner is awarded a compensation of Rs. 75,000/.
texts.arguments: In Ranu Bala Paul & Ors. v. Bani Chakraborty & Ors. 1999 ACJ 634, the Hon'ble Gawhati High Court has observed as under: "In deciding a matter tribunal should bear in mind the caution struck by the Apex Court that a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal is neither a criminal case nor a civil case. In a criminal case in order to have conviction, the matter is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt and in a civil case the matter is to be decided on the basis of preponderance of evidence, No doubt before the tribunal Shri Ravinder vs Shri Rajeev Kumar (Driver) on 5 February, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172549522/ 5 there must be some material on the basis of which the tribunal can arrive or decide things necessary to be decided for awarding compensation. After all, it is a summary inquiry and this is a legislation for the welfare of the society" 38. In the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Vijay Laxmi & Ors. MAC APP. No. 375/06 dated 05.07.12, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held as under: "8. In Bimla Devi and Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors., (2009) 13 SC 530, the Supreme Court held that in a petition under Section 166 of the Act, the Claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition under the Motor Vehicles Act. Para 15 of the report is extracted hereunder: "15. In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter. It was to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants. The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability. The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied." 9. The report in Bimla Devi (Supra) was relied on by the Supreme Court in its latest judgments in Parmeshwari v. Amir Chand (2011) 11 SCC 635 and Kusum Lata v. Satbir, (2011) 3 SCC 646." 39. In the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pushpa Rana & Ors.: 2009 ACJ 287, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that: "The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondentsclaimants should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard the counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meena Variyal (Supra). On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced: (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in F.I.R No. 955 of 2004, pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle; (ii) criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of chargesheet under Sections 279/304A, Indian Penal Code against the driver; (iii) certified copy of F.I.R., wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of the deceased. These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent. There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on the part of the driver." 40. This case was noticed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case titled as Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Kamlesh: 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310 where adverse inference was drawn because the driver of the offending vehicle had not appeared in the witness box to corroborate his defence taken in the written statement. Shri Ravinder vs Shri Rajeev Kumar (Driver) on 5 February, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172549522/ 6 41. . In the case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. ACJ 2011 (Vol. I), following principles were laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for determining compensation payable to road traffic accident victims: (i) The compensation payable to the claimant who is a victim of road accident should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equatable manner. (ii) Compensation payable in injury cases is payable under two heads. 53. In Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. v. Lalita: AIR 1981 Delhi 558, this Court held that there cannot be any deduction if domestic help is obtained from a family member. The High Court observed as under: "........... A wrong doer cannot take advantage of this 'domestic element'. If the mother renders service to her, instead of a nurse, it is right and just that she should recover compensation for the value of the services that the mother has rendered to her. Mother's services were necessitated by the wrong doing and the injured should be compensated for it. (Cunnigharn v. Harrison 3 All E.R. 463) The services of a wife and mother are worth more than those of a housekeeper because she is in constant attendance and does many more things than a housekeeper. (Regan v. Williamson (1976) 2 All E.R. 241)." 54. This judgment was again quoted with approval by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Narayan Bahadur v. Sumeet Gupta and Anr., MAC APP. No. 762/11 dated 04.07.12. 55. Considering the nature of injuries suffered by petitioner, it can be assumed that she would have availed services of an attendant at least for a period of three months. 56. Minimum wages payable to an unskilled workman on the date of accident were Rs. 5,278/. Therefore, this petitioner is awarded a compensation of Rs. 15,834/ towards Attendant Charges. 57. Petitioner has stated that she spent a sum of Rs. 81,505/ on medical treatment. In the case of Gulam Nabi Bhatt v. Mohd. Arman, MAC APP. No. 335/09 dated 07.08.12 the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi had awarded compensation for attendant's charges @ Rs. 2000/ per month for a period of 17 years to a claimant who was declared 100% permanently disabled in relation to both lower limbs. Relying on the case of Santosh Devi v. National Insurance Company Ltd. and others decided by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No. 3723 of 2012 arising out of SLP (C) No. 24489 of 10 dated 23.04.2012 and also relying on the case of Rakhi v. Satish Kumar & Ors. which is MAC APP. 79. Once 30% is added to Rs. 6,084/, loss of wages would be Rs. 7,909/ per month or Rs. 94,910/ p.a.
